name: Puvvah
overview: Puvvah is a male member of the tribe of Issachar, identified as a son of Issachar. He is listed among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking his place in the early history of the Israelite people. His inclusion in the Punite clan, as noted in the wilderness census, further establishes his tribal lineage within Israel.
namesAndTitles: The individual is primarily known as Puvvah, with variant spellings including Puvah and Puah. The name Puah is noted to possibly mean 'girl,' though this meaning is uncertain and not explicitly connected to him. None of the names are recorded as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Puvvah as a son of Issachar. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text concerning him.
scriptureSignificance: Puvvah's significance lies in his representation of the tribe of Issachar during the patriarchal migration to Egypt, a foundational event in Israel's history. His presence in the genealogical lists underscores the fulfillment of God's promises to the descendants of Jacob. Furthermore, his mention in the census of the Punites highlights the continuity of the tribal structure from the patriarchal period into the wilderness wanderings.
